problem: Prior GS-based real-to-sim navigation pipelines handle only static scenes or add dynamic obstacles as non-photorealistic simulator assets (e.g., Unity human meshes in Vid2Sim), which needs mesh extraction and a physics engine and leaves a visual gap for moving-human avoidance. General navigation models (GNM/ViNT/NoMaD) also underperform in environment-specific deployment.
motivation: Robots deployed in specific places (homes, restaurants, factories) must navigate safely around moving people using only RGB, but sim-to-real gaps and the cost of digital twins hinder this. A video-only reconstruction that includes photorealistic animated humans could produce environment-specific training data for dynamic navigation.
key_idea: Insert animatable human Gaussian-splat avatars, driven by a text-free motion diffusion model along planned 2D trajectories, into a reconstructed static GS scene, and use a dynamic-aware Hybrid A* expert to generate imitation data for a lightweight RGB-only policy.
insight: Vid2Sim and ReaDy-Go share the same policy architecture, human trajectories and expert planner and differ only in the dynamic obstacle representation. They perform similarly on Static tasks but diverge on Dynamic ones (e.g., Library sim 68% vs 80%; real Outside 60% vs 90%). This isolates photorealistic human GS as the source of the robustness gain. A 2M-parameter environment-specific policy also beats 30M-parameter ViNT, showing that scene-specific data matters more than model size.
method: Static GS reconstruction: metric-scale COLMAP poses (with an ArUco marker) from monocular video, followed by PGSR surface-regularized Gaussian splatting.

Human animation module: HUGS extracts animatable SMPL-based human GS avatars from NeuMan (6 avatars); PriorMDM converts a 2D trajectory (root velocities in HumanML3D format) to body motion, fitted to SMPL via SMPLify and placed in the world frame.

Voxelization with opacity filtering: occupied voxels come from 1-sigma Gaussian ellipsoids; voxels whose summed opacity is below a threshold are treated as free to remove floaters; projected into robot-navigable and human-walkable 2D maps with inflation.

Robot expert planner: Hybrid A* with motion primitives (3 velocity scales × 3 steering); human GS primitives with high covariance trace (above the 75th percentile) are removed, voxel-downsampled, projected, and inflated using 2 s constant-velocity prediction; reactive replanning is triggered periodically or when the distance to the human falls below a margin.
Human planner: samples start/goal pairs whose paths cross or run parallel to the robot's start-goal line, plans with A* and smooths with spline optimization, then animates the human.
Data generation: records RGB, expert actions (v, w) and relative goal for 400 episodes per environment (about 80–120k samples).

Policy: 10-layer residual CNN encoder (20-d) applied to 3 frames at 0.5 s intervals, concatenated with the previous action and relative goal, passed through a 3-layer MLP to output (v, w); trained by MSE imitation, 2M parameters, 144×256 input, 18 ms inference on Jetson Orin NX.

setting.backbone: Small ResNet-style CNN + MLP policy (trained from scratch, imitation learning)
setting.training_data: Synthetic expert demonstrations in GS simulator: 400 episodes per environment (~80–120k samples) from 6-minute monocular videos (1,000–1,500 images); 1,200 episodes combined for the generalization test
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (3 consecutive frames) + previous action + relative goal position from wheel odometry
setting.action_space: Continuous linear and angular velocity (v, w) for a unicycle robot
setting.simulator: Custom dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting simulator (PGSR scene + HUGS human avatars)
setting.privileged: Expert planner uses the GS-derived occupancy map and human GS for data generation only; none at test time (policy uses RGB + relative goal from odometry)

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only (three self-reconstructed environments), no standard benchmark. The number of episodes in the unseen-environment test is not stated. The expert planner reaches 100/91, 100/83 and 100/78% SR (Static/Dynamic) in Outside/Lobby/Library in simulation.
results: ReaDy-Go beats environment-specific Vid2Sim in Dynamic tasks (sim SR 78/78/80 vs 57/70/68 in Outside/Lobby/Library) and beats ViNT/GNM/NoMaD with 15× fewer parameters. In the real world it reaches 70–90% Dynamic SR versus 40–60% for Vid2Sim and 20–40% for ViNT. It also achieves 70% Static and 50% Dynamic SR zero-shot in an unseen real environment.
limitations: Only humans as dynamic agents, with modest densities (1–2 humans) and no aggressive motion; evaluated in only three environments with 10 real episodes each
Zero-shot generalization is limited (50–70% SR, longer times); the policy is environment-specific and needs a scene video per environment
Expert planner uses short-horizon constant-velocity prediction and does not reach 100% in Dynamic tasks (78–91%), which bounds the imitation quality
